t: Timbuktu began as a seasonal Tuareg camp near the Niger, and it grew into a trading town and a centre of Islamic learning as part of the Mali Empire from 1324 and then of the Songhai Empire from 1468 or 1469.

A Moroccan army captured the city on 30 May 1591, scholars were arrested, killed or exiled, and Timbuktu lost its standing as trade moved to Atlantic routes and its rulers changed many times until the French took it in 1893.
Its mosques are World Heritage monuments and its libraries hold manuscripts counted in the hundreds of thousands, which were threatened when armed groups held the city in 2012 and 2013.
dyk: During the occupation of the city by armed groups the librarian Abdel Kader Haidara had metal footlockers, each holding up to 300 manuscripts, distributed to nearly 2,500 safe houses in the city, and about 90% of the manuscripts were saved.
ev: The Tarikh al-Sudan dates the start of the seasonal Tuareg camp to the end of the fifth century of the hijra
Mansa Musa annexes Timbuktu to the Mali Empire on his return from pilgrimage to Mecca
Ibn Battuta visits Timbuktu and Kabara and meets the governor, Farba Musa
The Songhai Empire absorbs Timbuktu, in 1468 or 1469
A Moroccan army captures Timbuktu after the Battle of Tondibi
René Caillié reaches Timbuktu and returns to France to claim the Société de Géographie's prize
French soldiers under Lieutenant Gaston Boiteux annex the city
Tuareg rebels and Islamist groups take Timbuktu, and shrines are destroyed

f.founded: According to al-Sadi's Tarikh al-Sudan, a seasonal camp of the Maghsharan Tuareg about 1100 CE, which became a permanent town in the 13th or early 14th century; modern scholars hold that the evidence cannot fix the time or the founders.
f.where: 20 kilometres north of the Niger River, at the southern edge of the Sahara, in the Tombouctou Region of Mali.
f.known: The trans-Saharan trade in salt and gold; the Djinguereber, Sankoré and Sidi Yahya mosques; its scholars and manuscripts; Mansa Musa and Askia Mohammad I; the Moroccan conquest of 1591; the accounts of Leo Africanus and René Caillié
f.today: Timbuktu is the capital of Mali's Tombouctou Region, with about eighty thousand people.
